decisions.reason: Tooling for a dedicated harvesting crate is already sunk and it fits the announced agricultural reusable-packaging direction, so management will treat weak first-year visibility as a temporary ramp-up effect.
The foldable large container has its own web page, sits at the core of the firm's reusable logistics strategy and carries heavy mould investment, so the firm is strongly committed to it.
A stackable crate is a low-risk core range item with sunk tooling, and dropping it after one year would undercut the earlier launch decision.
The rackable pallet fills a gap in the core pallet line, and its expensive injection tooling encourages management to persist and attribute slow uptake to market ramp-up.
Presenting the spill-retention pallet on its own page signals public commitment to an industrial niche, so management will keep it and expect results to improve.
The pallet with load retainers is publicly promoted on a dedicated page and extends the core pallet range, so sunk costs and visible commitment favor keeping it.
